cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. When you call the picnic a success, what are you measuring?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And how do I rank against last year's organiser?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does your clipboard have last year's sandwich total?

mechanism: A presides over the evaluation itself and demands the criteria, B stake and A comparative position before allowing a vague success claim to stand.
confusable: Generic suspicion of motives is confusable: the dialogue must pursue measurement, B gain and A rank, not just one of those elements.
comparison: Picnic organizer questions evaluation used for an evaluator budget renewal; election candidate tests competence language against a voter pet project and ranking.
seedUse: Read both cards and all four seeds critically: canonical a lacks B gain, canonical b lacks A rank. Use exact full instruction rather than assume each partial seed covers the whole pursuit.
